title: The Book in the Rubble
subtitle: A sermon on Huldah
big_idea: The word of God found in the rubble wounds the proud, hears the humble, and points to the King who took its curse: Huldah spoke the word, Josiah reformed the nation, and Jesus bore the judgment.

start_here_runtime: 57 minutes with the full response; 55–60 with normal variation. The manuscript is 6,858 words at about 120 words per minute.
start_here_cut: If you have 50 minutes: Introduction to 4, Movement 1 to 6, Movement 2 to 7, Movement 3 to 7, Movement 4 to 6, Movement 5 to 7, Application to 5. Keep 2 Kings 22:19–20, the tender heart, Megiddo, 2 Kings 23:26–27, Galatians 3:13, and the empty tomb.
start_here_guardrails: Do not invent the discovery scene or Huldah’s biography. The text gives the delegation, the names, the Second Quarter, and the oracle.
Say “widely identified with Deuteronomy or a core of it,” not “we know exactly what the scroll was.”
Do not turn “a grave in peace” into a prosperity promise. Josiah died in battle at Megiddo.
Note Huldah’s significance without making her a slogan; label rabbinic traditions as later tradition.
The gospel must be explicit: the cross, the resurrection, and the new heart. Do not end on “read your Bible more.”
Keep the pastoral care note for victims and the call to safety; do not rush to “reform” language over a wound.
start_here_evidence: The discovery of the Book of the Law, Huldah’s oracle, the king’s tender heart, and the reform that could not turn away the wrath are doing theological work, and the cross and the empty tomb are the turn.

slides.run: A SERMON FOR THE PULPIT · 55–60 MINUTES

slides.label: 01 · THE BIG IDEA
slides.note: The word that wounds is the word that heals.

slides.label: 02 · THE FIND
slides.headline: The house of the LORD had a book it had forgotten.
panel: The book was in the house.
The word was not in the heart.
slides.kicker: A routine repair became a national reckoning.

slides.label: 03 · THE DELEGATION
slides.headline: Who do you send for when the book finds you?

slides.label: 04 · THE PROPHETESS
slides.headline: Five men went to the Second Quarter.
slides.body: The high priest, the secretary, the king’s servant, and two senior officials walked across the city to a woman who spoke for God. The word was not in the palace or the temple. It was in the newer part of town.
slides.pullquote: “Tell the man who sent you to me.”
slides.footline: The messenger is tested by the message.

slides.label: 05 · THE OBJECTION
slides.headline: Is a tender heart enough?
slides.quote: “I have the book. Isn’t that enough?”
slides.aside1: The book was in the house of the LORD, and the nation had forgotten it.
slides.aside2: Hearing is not the same as obeying.
slides.footline: God hears the heart that trembles at His word.

slides.label: 06 · THE WORD
slides.footline: Huldah did not soften the first or universalize the second.

slides.label: 07 · THE PROMISE
slides.banner_main: “Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD… I also have heard you, declares the LORD.”
slides.footline: He was gathered before he saw the fall.

slides.label: 08 · THE GREATER KING
slides.banner_main: “Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us.”
slides.footline: The law could not save. The King could.

slides.label: 09 · THE RESPONSE
slides.headline: What do you do with a book that finds you?
